notes: COUNTING RULES (IOM methodology page): the project counts people who die 'at the external borders of states' or 'in the process of migration towards an international destination', whatever their legal status, from shipwrecks, transport accidents, violence, harsh conditions etc.; it excludes deaths in immigration detention and deaths after a migrant is established in a new home. 'Number dead' = bodies recovered; 'Number missing' = people missing and assumed dead, usually computed for shipwrecks by subtracting bodies recovered and survivors from the reported number aboard, often from survivor or witness testimony; 'Total dead and missing' is the sum of the two. In large shipwrecks IOM uses the minimum number reported on board. IOM states its data are a minimum estimate and that at sea many bodies are never recovered. IOM publishes no statistical estimate of unrecorded deaths. 'INVISIBLE SHIPWRECKS' is IOM's term for entire boats reported missing with no information on rescue or interception ever found. For 2025 IOM counted 'at least 1,500' such unverified reports on sea routes to Europe (730 Atlantic, 400 Western Mediterranean) and kept them OUT of its confirmed totals; the ledger's '~1,500 estimated in unrecorded wrecks' is this unverified count, not an estimate, and its high=5,700 wrongly adds it. The only other 'invisible shipwrecks' figure IOM prints is an NGO's (Caminando Fronteras) 2023 Atlantic estimate, which IOM calls unverifiable. AS-OF DATES: 2025 route figures are from IOM's 2025 Annual Global Report, 'All data in this report is as of 1 March 2026' (published 21 April 2026 as an ArcGIS StoryMap; body text read from the ArcGIS item JSON endpoint, which a reviewer can open in a browser). The report prints no 2025 Mediterranean total; 2,185 and 1,214 are from a UN briefing of 26 February 2026. 2024 figures: IOM press release 21 March 2025 (data as of 20 March 2025) and IOM GMDAC's Migration Data Portal (frozen March 2025), plus 2024 comparisons in the 2025 report; IOM's own values for 2024 changed between these dates (Caribbean 341 to 302; global 8,938 to 9,191 to nearly 9,200). 2023 figures: IOM decade report, database accessed 13 March 2024 (Mediterranean 3,105; the portal later shows 3,155 and a January 2024 release said 3,041). GAPS: Eastern/Western Mediterranean 2023, Bay of Bengal 2023 and 2024, English Channel 2023, exact Central/Western Mediterranean 2024 and 2025 were not found in any document that opened; the MMP 2024 blog and the live route dashboards should fill them. The portal home page served to this run was a stale render (latest incident 16 October 2024) so its table values carry an uncertain as-of date. Route names as IOM prints them: 'Central Mediterranean', 'Eastern Mediterranean', 'Western Mediterranean' (crossing), 'Western Africa/Atlantic Route to the Spanish Canary Islands' / 'the Canary Islands route', 'Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea', 'the route from mainland Europe to the United Kingdom, including the English Channel crossing' (portal label 'English Channel to the UK'), 'Caribbean', 'the sea crossing to Yemen' (portal 'Eastern Route'). No figure in this bundle was summed by the agent; the 3,400 and over 3,800 aggregates are IOM's own. Also seen but not rowed: IOM's decade report gives 4,470 drowning deaths worldwide in 2023 (Section 1.6, p. 9) without a verbatim quote captured; worth a follow-up for the drowning layer.
